transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Monday, October 19. transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Babar Azam achieves historic milestone, joins Inzamam and Miandad in elite list. The match against Sri Lanka was his 355th in international cricket. However, he fell short of a half-century, getting out for 45 to Pavan Rathnayake off Eshan Malinga. US-designated LeT terrorist dies after mysteriously falling from building in Lahore. Chaudhry Mohammad Sarwar, a prominent terrorist of Lashkar-e-Taiba, recently died after falling from a building in Lahore. Known for his role in fundraising for the group, he was involved in various leadership positions. Previously designated a terrorist by the US, he had connections with senior leaders like Hafiz Saeed. Sarwar's death occurred under mysterious circumstances, similar to a past incident involving another notable figure. Amazon threatens to pull 5,000 delivery jobs out of New York City over Mamdani's bill. Amazon has warned it could shut 15 warehouses and move thousands of delivery jobs out of New York City over the Delivery Protection Act, a labour bill backed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani. The bill would require Amazon to directly employ 5,000 contracted delivery drivers. Logistics experts say the retail giant is likely to follow through, pointing to its decision to close seven warehouses in Montreal, Canada, after a union drive. Indiana daughter loses will challenge, ordered to pay $22,208 in legal fees. An Indiana woman who challenged her late father's decision to leave his entire estate to his fiancee has lost her legal battle. Stacia Davis was ordered to pay $22,208 in attorney fees after failing to prove the will was invalid. The Indiana Court of Appeals upheld the ruling and ordered her to pay additional legal fees after finding serious problems with her appeal. Shinde meets Tiger Shroff after firing incident; pics show actor with bandages. Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde met Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff at his residence on Sunday night after a firing incident in Mumbai's Juhu area, assuring the actor and his family of the state government's support. Milan on edge: Protesters clash with cops, smash windows; videos show chaos. Milan descended into chaos on Sunday as hundreds of masked protesters clashed with police, smashed shop windows and looted stores in the city centre, with videos showing tense scenes around the iconic Piazza del Duomo. Tiger Shroff covers face, reaches home under police protection after Juhu firing. Tiger Shroff was escorted home under police protection after unidentified attackers fired three shots at his car in Mumbai's Juhu on Sunday, October 18, 2026, as he returned from football. He was unhurt, though tape on his hand drew attention. His driver was injured. A message linked to the Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility; police haven't verified it. Almost a century after J and K HC was set up, Ladakh gets bench. Almost a century after the establishment of Jammu and Kashmir HC, the Union Territory of Ladakh Sunday got a high court bench, which will sit in Leh, 3,500 metres above sea level , an altitude no other HC can ever match. Elephant deaths transform grasslands for 8 years, study finds. A study in South Africa's Kruger National Park reveals that elephant carcasses can transform grasslands long after the animals die. Research inspired by the death of a great tusker named Alexander found that soil nitrogen levels at fresh carcass sites can rise up to 3,000 times, creating nutrient hotspots that attract grazing animals for at least eight years. Seattle's buried streets: Tour the city under Pioneer Square. In June 1889, a catastrophic fire reshaped Seattle, prompting city officials to elevate street levels to address mud and sanitation issues for local merchants. This led to the creation of underground areas, which served various functions until they were shuttered for health reasons in 1907. The 1960s saw a revival of interest in Pioneer Square's history, resulting in restored areas now accessible to the public while ensuring safety and preservation.

transcript.title: Money, tax and personal finance
transcript.text: Now to your money — taxes, savings and personal finance. SIP or STP for PMS investments? Key differences, costs and risks investors should know before choosing. The rising inclination toward systematic investment plans (SIPs) for Portfolio Management Services (PMS) is becoming increasingly visible among Indian investors. A notable percentage of PMS strategies are starting to incorporate SIPs for regular investments. Particularly, younger investors looking to build wealth are favouring this approach to mitigate market risks. With recent regulatory shifts regarding PRIM, advancements in technology and education for investors are essential for broader adoption of PMS SIPs. Got refund for online shopping after cancelling order but your credit card bill still shows due amount? Should you pay?. Here's what to do if your billing date is near but the refund has not been credited yet. NBFC stocks in focus: Rising funding costs threaten margins despite robust loan growth and asset quality. Analysts emphasize that successfully managing these costs will be key to sustaining growth, advising cautious investment in resilient NBFCs amid changing market dynamics. The three-bucket strategy can help people achieving financial independence and early retirement (FIRE) manage expenses and market volatility.
